questions.stem: Which is the correct ascending order of Bloom's Revised Taxonomy?

options.B: Understand→Remember→Apply→Create→Analyse→Evaluate
options.C: Remember→Apply→Understand→Evaluate→Analyse→Create
options.D: Apply→Remember→Understand→Analyse→Create→Evaluate

questions.explanation: Anderson & Krathwohl (2001) revised the taxonomy into six ascending levels: Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyse, Evaluate, Create.
questions.source: Anderson & Krathwohl. A Taxonomy for Learning, Teaching, and Assessing. Pearson, 2001. https://www.bloomstaxonomy.net

questions.stem: Which cognitive verbs are associated with Bloom's Level 1 (Remember)?

options.B: Design, construct, develop, produce
options.C: Define, identify, list, recall, state
options.D: Classify, compare, explain, interpret

questions.explanation: L1 (Remember) targets retrieval of previously learned information. Verbs: define, identify, list, memorise, recall, repeat, state.
questions.source: Anderson & Krathwohl. A Taxonomy for Learning. 2001.

questions.stem: 'Explain why a sorted array is required for binary search.' At which Bloom level does this operate?

options.B: L2 — requires explaining the principle connecting sorting to the algorithm's logic
options.C: L3 — requires implementing binary search
options.D: L4 — requires evaluating search algorithm efficiency

questions.explanation: 'Explain' and connecting a precondition to a mechanism requires understanding (L2). No implementation (L3) or comparative evaluation (L4) is asked.
questions.source: Anderson & Krathwohl. A Taxonomy for Learning. 2001.

questions.stem: How do Bloom's L5 (Evaluate) and L6 (Create) differ in cognitive demand?

options.A: L5 requires memorisation; L6 requires computation
options.B: L5 requires judgements based on criteria and evidence; L6 requires synthesising elements into a novel coherent whole
options.C: Both require only recall from multiple sources
options.D: L5 = procedural knowledge; L6 = declarative knowledge

questions.explanation: L5: learners judge using standards. L6: learners produce something new by combining knowledge. L6 is the highest cognitive demand.
questions.source: Anderson & Krathwohl. A Taxonomy for Learning. 2001.

questions.stem: Which of the following best exemplifies a Bloom's L3 (Apply) question on gradient descent?

options.B: Explain how learning rate affects convergence.
options.C: Trace three iterations of gradient descent on f(w)=w²−4w+5 starting at w=0 with α=0.5, showing each weight update and loss value.
options.D: Evaluate whether Adam is superior to SGD for all deep learning tasks.

questions.explanation: A=L1, B=L2, D=L5. C requires executing the algorithm step-by-step — computing ∂L/∂w and applying w←w−α·∂L/∂w — which is L3 Apply. At w=0: ∂L/∂w=−4; w₁=2. At w=2: ∂L/∂w=0; converged.

mini_quizzes.title: MQ-2 · Memory, Forgetting, and Retrieval Practice

questions.stem: What does the Ebbinghaus Forgetting Curve describe?

options.A: Relationship between study time and exam scores
options.B: Exponential decay of memory retention over time without rehearsal
options.C: Linear growth of long-term memory through repeated exposure
options.D: Cognitive load imposed by new material in a single session

questions.explanation: Ebbinghaus (1885) found retention decays exponentially: ~58% after 20 min, ~44% after 1 hour, ~25% after 1 week. This forms the empirical basis for spaced repetition.

questions.stem: Roediger & Karpicke (2006) found which strategy produced significantly better long-term retention than re-reading?

options.B: Summarising notes in a different colour
options.C: Retrieval practice — recalling information via testing
options.D: Listening to lectures at 1.5× speed

questions.explanation: The testing effect: students who practised retrieval retained ~50% more at a 1-week delayed test. Retrieving strengthens the memory trace more than passive re-exposure.

questions.stem: Why does spaced repetition produce better long-term retention than cramming, even with equal total study time?

options.A: Spaced repetition uses more colourful materials
options.B: Cramming activates only short-term memory; spaced repetition is impossible digitally
options.C: Each spaced retrieval resets the forgetting curve and strengthens the memory trace; massed practice benefits fade rapidly
options.D: Spaced repetition increases total hours studied

questions.explanation: Each successful retrieval after a delay partially resets the forgetting curve and re-encodes memory more durably. 5×1-hour spaced sessions retain ~3× more at 2 weeks than one 5-hour massed session.
questions.source: Ebbinghaus. 1885; Cepeda et al. Psychological Bulletin, 2006.

questions.stem: A student scores 90% immediately after a lecture but 40% two weeks later. What does this indicate, and what is the most evidence-based intervention?

options.B: Quiz too difficult — reduce difficulty
options.C: Normal forgetting curve decay; prescribe spaced retrieval at day 1, 3, 7, and 14 post-learning
options.D: Student inattentive — replay the lecture

questions.explanation: 90%→40% over two weeks is consistent with Ebbinghaus's exponential forgetting curve. The remedy: spaced retrieval at expanding intervals to reset the curve before severe forgetting.

questions.stem: Designing a spaced repetition schedule for 50 Python syntax rules, 30 min/day for 4 weeks. Which schedule best applies evidence-based spacing principles?

options.A: Study all 50 on Day 1; spend remaining days on other subjects
options.B: Study 12–13 new rules each week in a single weekly block
options.C: Introduce ~7 rules daily, review previous rules at expanding intervals (Day+1, +3, +7, +14) using flashcard retrieval
options.D: Read all 50 rules aloud every day for 4 weeks

questions.explanation: Option C applies: (1) distributed introduction to avoid overload; (2) expanding-interval spacing to reset forgetting curves; (3) retrieval practice over passive re-reading. Options A/B mass study; D uses passive re-reading.

questions.stem: In Sweller's CLT, which load type refers to the inherent difficulty of the material?

options.B: Germane cognitive load
options.C: Intrinsic cognitive load
options.D: Transient cognitive load

questions.explanation: Intrinsic load is determined by content complexity — the number of interacting elements held in working memory. Manageable by simple→complex sequencing but not eliminable.

questions.stem: Which type of cognitive load should instructional designers aim to MINIMISE?

options.B: Germane load
options.C: Extraneous load
options.D: Affective load

questions.explanation: Extraneous load is caused by poor instructional design — irrelevant info, unclear layouts, redundant explanations. It consumes working memory without contributing to schema formation.

questions.stem: A tutorial presents a 500-word paragraph, three unrelated code snippets, two pop-up ads, and a scrolling ticker simultaneously. Which load type is imposed and what is its effect?

options.A: Intrinsic — programming complexity fills working memory
options.B: Germane — processing irrelevant content builds schemas
options.C: Extraneous — poor design forces irrelevant processing, consuming working memory and reducing learning
options.D: Affective — emotional distraction reduces motivation

questions.explanation: Ads, scrolling text, and unrelated snippets impose extraneous load — working memory spent on irrelevant material reduces resources for understanding programming content.
questions.source: Sweller. 1988; Mayer. Multimedia Learning. Cambridge UP, 2001.

questions.stem: How does germane cognitive load differ from extraneous load in its effect on learning?

options.A: Both harmful and should be minimised
options.B: Germane promotes schema construction and should be maximised; extraneous wastes working memory and should be minimised
options.C: Germane = content difficulty; extraneous = student anxiety
options.D: They are identical constructs with different names

questions.explanation: Germane load is productive cognitive effort building schemas — beneficial. Extraneous arises from poor design and wastes capacity. Goal: minimise extraneous, manage intrinsic, maximise germane.

questions.stem: Evaluate this question: 'Considering the socioeconomic, historical, technological, geopolitical, and neuroscientific contexts of ML since 1943, explain in 800 words how intrinsic load manifests when novices learn backpropagation.' Identify the primary flaw and fix.

options.A: No flaw — rich multi-context maximises germane load for beginners
options.B: Excessive extraneous load: five irrelevant contexts and 800-word demand. Fix: 'Describe two ways intrinsic load manifests when a novice encounters backpropagation.'
options.C: Insufficient intrinsic load — too easy for advanced learners
options.D: Uses 'explain' instead of 'define' — wrong Bloom level

questions.explanation: Five contextual framing elements are extraneous — irrelevant to the core question, consuming working memory. The fix strips extraneous framing and keeps a clear L2 cognitive demand.

mini_quizzes.title: MQ-4 · Assessment Design and AI in Education

questions.stem: Which best defines formative assessment?

options.A: High-stakes final examination counting toward a grade
options.B: Ongoing, low-stakes assessment used to monitor progress and provide feedback during instruction
options.C: Standardised national test administered once per year
options.D: Portfolio collected at course end

questions.explanation: Formative assessment is assessment FOR learning — during instruction, low-stakes, providing actionable feedback. Contrasts with summative (assessment OF learning at course endpoint).
questions.source: Black & Wiliam. Phi Delta Kappan, 1998; U.S. Dept. of Education. 2010. https://www2.ed.gov/rschstat/eval/tech/evidence-based-practices/finalreport.pdf

questions.stem: Bloom's 2-sigma problem (1984) found tutored students performed how many standard deviations above classroom-instructed students?

options.B: 1.0 SD
options.C: 2.0 SD
options.D: 3.5 SD

questions.explanation: Bloom (1984) found the average tutored student outperformed 98% of conventionally instructed students — a 2 SD advantage, motivating AI-driven adaptive learning.

questions.stem: Why is formative assessment more powerful for improving learning than summative assessment alone?

options.B: Provides timely, specific feedback students can act on during learning, closing gaps before summative evaluation
options.C: Requires less instructor preparation
options.D: Summative is only used in higher education

questions.explanation: Black & Wiliam (1998) meta-analysis: formative assessment effect sizes 0.4–0.7 SD — among the highest educational interventions. Mechanism: specific timely feedback allows correcting misconceptions while content is still being taught.

questions.stem: How does an Intelligent Tutoring System differ from a static e-learning course in personalisation?

options.B: ITS dynamically adapts difficulty, pacing, and feedback to each learner's knowledge state; static courses deliver the same sequence to all
options.C: Static courses are more expensive to develop
options.D: Both deliver identical experiences — only cost differs

questions.explanation: An ITS models student knowledge (student model), selects optimal instructional actions (pedagogical model), and gives immediate targeted feedback — approximating Bloom's 2-sigma effect. Static courses present a fixed sequence.

questions.stem: Designing a 5-question mini-quiz on Python list comprehensions at Beginner level with 2:2:1 Bloom ratio. Which set is correctly structured?

options.A: 5 questions: define, state, list, name, recall — all L1
options.B: Q1: Define list comprehension (L1). Q2: Identify syntax of [x**2 for x in range(5)] (L1). Q3: Explain why comprehensions are faster than for-loops (L2). Q4: Describe a readability use case (L2). Q5: Write a comprehension returning even squares from [1,2,3,4,5,6] (L3).
options.C: 5 questions all asking to write code at L3
options.D: Q1–Q2: Evaluate/Design (L5–L6); Q3–Q5: Recall

questions.explanation: Option B: Q1–Q2 L1, Q3–Q4 L2, Q5 L3 — correct 2:2:1 ratio with appropriate difficulty escalation for Beginners. A=all L1; C=all L3; D=inappropriate L5–L6 for Beginners.
questions.source: Anderson & Krathwohl. A Taxonomy for Learning. 2001.
